content:
maya: Heads-up — LarkPay reported a ~30% throughput drop on their dedicated pool starting ~02:15 UTC after the canary deploy. They see sustained queueing and lower tokens/sec. tagging @sam & @devon for triage :wave:
sam: oncall looped in, looking at ingestion logs now. Do we know which model variant they're pinned to?
maya: LarkPay is pinned to redwood/llama-13b-qat:v2 (quantized). perf-bot earlier showed the canary used the new kernel selector heuristics.
perf-bot: Deploy 2026-02-10T02:10Z applied to pool larkpay-dedicated with kernel-selector=v2. Canary traffic ramped to 10%. No immediate errors logged.
devon: ok i'll pull the pool metrics and run a micro-bench against that variant. Can someone paste the customer request pattern?
irene: customer provided sample qps and sequence lengths: 120 qps steady-state, 1.2k tokens/session average, many short prefix hits (lots of prefix reuse).
cj: quick check: p95 latency jumped from 35ms -> 120ms around 02:17 according to console graphs. Throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~28%.
luis: copying the raw tail of the runtime agent logs I got from their account: ```
[02:16:58] rpc: queue_size=87 inflight=60 dispatch_ms=15
[02:17:03] scheduler: batch_wait=42ms median, batching_rate=0.72
[02:17:05] kernel_selector: chosen_variant=quantized_fast (latency_pref=balanced)
[02:17:10] kvcache: hit_rate=0.62 miss_penalty=18ms
```
devon: looks like batching/backpressure is increasing. Can you also grab GPU utilization and max_cta stats from the hosts?
sam: grabbing host stats now — reply from one worker: ```
GPU0 util 88% mem 72% sm_eff 0.81 active_cta 24
GPU1 util 65% mem 69% sm_eff 0.54 active_cta 14
IO wait spiked to 12% at 02:16:xx
```
maya: interesting mismatch between GPUs. Could be uneven routing or a bad kernel fallback. @devon can you run a targeted bench that mimics their prefix-heavy workload? Suggest: `runt-bench --model redwood/llama-13b-qat:v2 --qps 120 --seq-profile prefix-heavy --duration 6m --pin-pool larkpay-dedicated`
devon: starting that now on my laptop against a canary node. Also enabling kernel selector debug: `EXPORT RW_DEBUG_KERNEL=1` to capture decision traces.
(10m later)
devon: bench shows throughput oscillations when kvcache hit_rate ~60-65%. I captured kernel selector logs: it toggles between `quantized_fast` and `quantized_fallback` every ~30s which forces recompile/warm paths. excerpt: ```
[KS] 02:17:28 candidate=quantized_fast score=0.78
[KS] 02:17:29 candidate=quantized_fallback score=0.81 reason=mem_pressure
[KS] 02:17:58 switch -> reinit kernels (cost 120ms)
```
irene: that explains the throughput drop — warm reinit cost added to tail repeatedly. Why is mem_pressure flipping?
devon: likely scheduler batching creating transient high memory + aggressive prefetch heuristics in v2. If one worker hits a fallback, clients get routed away and other workers see burst load.
maya: pragmatic fix: roll kernel-selector back to v1 for the LarkPay pool while we root cause. Can we do a canary rollout?
sam: yes we can. Suggest policy: pin 25% of nodes to kernel-selector=v1, 75% remain v2 for 15m, measure tokens/s and p95. I'll prepare the rollout and metrics dashboard.
cj: i'll set up a short alert to notify if tokens/s improves <15% within 20m. Also add a trace to capture per-worker kernel-switch events.
luis: customer update drafted: "We're investigating a transient throughput regression after a recent runtime optimization. We're running targeted profiling and a controlled rollback to stabilize throughput. Will update in 30m." Want me to send?
maya: go ahead and send. devon, after rollback can you also create a minimized repro and open an issue with kernel-selector logs + env?
devon: yes — i'll upload logs to the incident bucket and link the issue. steps: 1) bench artifact + kernel logs 2) per-host perf counters 3) kvcache traces 4) timeline.
perf-bot: Canary rollback scheduled by @sam: target pool=larkpay-dedicated, change kernel-selector -> v1, rollout 25% -> 100% in 20m.
sam: rollback started at 02:45. first 25% swapped, monitoring.
(10m later)
cj: early numbers: tokens/s improved ~18% on the nodes with v1. p95 on those nodes down to ~40ms. Overall pool improved ~12% so far.
maya: great. we'll keep v1 on for now and open an RFC for safer kernel switching heuristics. Action items: sam own rollback + monitor until 03:15, devon capture repro and file issue, cj add metric alert and trace, luis send customer update at 03:00.
sam: ack.
devon: ack, will push logs in ~30m.
maya: thanks everyone — update thread when we have final numbers. :thumbsup:
